==English==
{{wp}}
[[File:Wallinger Avenue.jpg|thumb|Snowy road on Overwaitea Hill, Wallinger Avenue, Kimberley, BC.]]

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|rade||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|rode|id=ride}}, {{m|enm|rade|id=ride|t=ride, journey}}, from {{inh|en|ang|rād||riding, hostile incursion}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*raidu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*raidō||a ride}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*reydʰ-||to ride}}. {{doublet|en|raid}}, acquired from {{cog|sco|-}}. Cognates include West Frisian {{m|fy|reed}} (paved trail/road, driveway).

The current primary meaning of "street, way for traveling"  originated relatively late — Shakespeare seemed to expect his audiences to find it unfamiliar — and probably arose through reinterpretation of {{m|en|roadway||a way for riding on}} as saying {{m|en|way}} twice, in other words as a [[tautological]] [[compound]].

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q34442}} A [[way]] used for [[travel]]ling between places, originally one wide enough to allow foot passengers and horses to travel, now (US) usually one [[surface]]d with [[asphalt]] or [[concrete]] and designed to accommodate many [[vehicle]]s travelling in both directions. In the UK both senses are heard: a country road is the same as a country [[lane]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1852|author=Mrs M.A. Thompson|chapter=The Tutor's Daughter|title=Graham's American Monthly Magazine of Literature, Art, and Fashion|page=266|url=http://books.google.com/books?id=hdcRAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA266
|passage=In the lightness of my heart I sang catches of songs as my horse gayly bore me along the well-remembered '''road'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=1|passage=I stumbled along through the young pines and huckleberry bushes. Pretty soon I struck into a sort of path that, I cal'lated, might lead to the '''road''' I was hunting for.}}
#* {{quote-song|1=en|year=2018|author=Bill Wurtz|title=Long Long Long Journey|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0jEm6owSKFU|text=And the '''road''' doesn't end / It's a long, long '''road''' and we follow it again and again / And the '''road''' don't pretend}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} Roads in general as a means of travel, especially by [[motor vehicle]].
#: {{ux|en|We travelled to the seaside by '''road'''.}}
# {{lb|en|dated}} A physical way or route.
#* {{RQ:Dickens Little Dorrit|passage=He stirred up his hair with his sprightliest expression, glanced at the little figure again, said ‘Good evening, ma ‘am; don’t come down, Mrs Affery, I know the '''road''' to the door,’ and steamed out.}}
#* {{RQ:Lindsay Redheap|page=131|passage=Hetty and Mrs. Piper watched them with a lynx-eyed understanding and before the ancient was well upon his '''road''' his way was blocked by Hetty.}}
# {{lb|en|figuratively}} A [[path]] chosen, as in [[life]] or [[career]]. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|the '''road''' to happiness; the '''road''' to success.}}
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1964|author=Ronald Reagan|title=A Time for Choosing
|passage=Where, then, is the '''road''' to peace?}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=September 7, 2012|author=Phil McNulty|work=BBC Sport
|title=[http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/19460608 Moldova 0-5 England]
|passage=Hodgson may actually feel England could have scored even more but this was the perfect first step on the '''road''' to Rio in 2014 and the ideal platform for the second qualifier against Ukraine at Wembley on Tuesday.}}
# An underground [[tunnel]] in a [[mine]]. {{defdate|from 18th c.}}
# {{senseid|en|Q22667}} {{lb|en|US|railroads|archaic}} A [[railroad]].<!--[[railroad]] was usually viewed as hyponymous to [[road]] in the 19th century through the mid-20th, which is why railroads were often called roads in that era, but since then it usually is not-->
# {{senseid|en|Q160342}} {{lb|en|US|UK|railroads}} A single [[railroad track]] ([[railway track]]). {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1959|month=November|title=L.T. and E.R. developments in East London|journal=Trains Illustrated|page=527|text=The new depot, on which work started in May, 1956, has three reception '''roads''' leading to 13 sidings capable of taking 25 trains, a 450 ft.-long car examination shed with nine '''roads''', a lifting shop with two '''roads''' and three permanent way sidings.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} The act of [[riding]] on [[horseback]]. {{defdate|9th|17th c.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[hostile]] [[ride]] against a particular area; a [[raid]]. {{defdate|9th|19th c.}}
# {{senseid|en|nautical}} {{lb|en|nautical|usually|in the plural}} A partly [[sheltered]] area of water near a shore in which [[vessel]]s may ride at [[anchor]]; a [[roadstead]]. {{defdate|from 14th c.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|V|i|text={{smallcaps|Antonio}}: Sweet lady, you have given me life and living; / For here I read for certain that my ships / Are safely come to '''road'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1630|author={{w|John Smith (explorer)|John Smith}}|title=True Travels|publisher=Kupperman|year_published=1988|page=38
|passage=There delivering their fraught, they went to Scandaroone; rather to view what ships was in the '''Roade''', than any thing else […].}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A journey, or stage of a journey.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 8|IV|ii|text=At last, with easy '''roads''', he came to Leicester; / Lodg'd in the abbey, where the reverend abbot, / With all his convent, honourably receiv'd him; {{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|cricket}} A [[hard]], [[flat]] [[pitch]], typically favourable for [[batter]]s.

====Usage notes====
* Often used interchangeably with {{m|en|street}} or other similar words. When usage is distinguished, a road is a route between settlements (reflecting the etymological relation with {{m|en|ride}}), as in the {{w|Great North Road (Great Britain)|Great North Road}} from London to Edinburgh, while a street is a route within a settlement (city or town), strictly speaking, paved.

====Hyponyms====
* See also [[Thesaurus:road]]
